candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members and participate in quality-improvement systems to promote safe client care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary antimicrobial stewardship
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize antimicrobial stewardship as a multidisciplinary care-management function in which trained pharmacy expertise participates in program leadership, antimicrobial review, and active prescribing interventions rather than being limited to medication dispensing.

options.A: Use physician-pharmacist stewardship leadership, with trained pharmacy expertise participating in program management and interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization.
options.B: Limit the pharmacist to medication dispensing and exclude pharmacy expertise from antimicrobial-use decisions.
options.C: Assign stewardship responsibility to nursing alone and avoid collaboration with physicians or pharmacists so accountability remains with one discipline.
options.D: Use pharmacy expertise only after an antimicrobial course is complete because stewardship interventions should not influence active prescribing.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's current Hospital Core Elements identify accountability and pharmacy expertise as core stewardship components and note that many effective programs are co-led by a physician and pharmacist. CDC also recommends active stewardship interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization. Current 2026 multi-society guidance likewise describes stewardship as multidisciplinary and emphasizes clinical infectious-diseases, pharmacology, microbiology, quality-improvement, communication, and program-evaluation skills. B and D improperly reduce the pharmacist to a dispensing role. C conflicts with the collaborative program structure recommended by CDC.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current stewardship guidance supports active physician-pharmacist leadership and trained pharmacy participation in antimicrobial-use interventions and program management rather than a dispensing-only role.
